messages:
anna: quick check — i'm prototyping two patterns for private control plane connectivity for Private customers: (A) regional aggregator (one cp-endpoint per-region that peers into customer VPCs) vs (B) per-tenant lightweight stub running in-customer that tunnels back. want quick tradeoffs + operational gotchas before i write an RFC.

sam: +1. my quick take: aggregator gives easier ops (single cert set, single routing policy) but amplifies blast radius and complicates subnet/route quotas. stub gives isolation but is a deployment burden and harder to debug.

tara: DNS/certs are a big hidden cost. if we do aggregator we need short TTLs & per-tenant SANs or SNI passthrough. otherwise cert churn for many tenants will be awful. :frowning:

jess: also consider cost/unit: aggregator -> fewer cross-account VPC peering attachments but more egress from our regional VPCs; stub -> more attachments, potential AWS attachment limits per account. we'll need a cost model.

mohit: technical note: MTU and TCP path MTU discovery across a tunnel matter. stubs that use GRE or VXLAN + encapsulation often hit MSS blackholing for long tokens. tested this with our internal relay spike — ended up forcing TCP MSS clamp on the tunnel.

anna: good call. do we have a preference on auth model? i was leaning to per-tenant mTLS identities issued by our CA so aggregator can still do RBAC per-tenant.

sam: per-tenant mTLS is nice but then aggregator becomes an authorization gateway — need to make sure token mapping -> customer-id is always idempotent. race conditions in cert rotation caused a few incidents in the past (see link). <https://go/rfc-private-cp-agg>

tara: operational edge-case: hairpinning. if aggregator lives in same region and we NAT back into the customer VPC, we need careful route table entries to avoid asymmetric paths. i've seen conntrack exhaustion when NAT rules overlap.

jess: rollout suggestion: start with aggregator but limit scope via a canary org + explicit route table automation. deploy a control-plane fallback to public-hosted endpoints for non-critical traffic. rollback path needs to be a 1-command cut. :white_check_mark:

mohit: another option — hybrid: aggregator for small customers, stub for large/regulated. we can automate stub bootstrap via tenant onboarding pipeline (cloudformation / terraform module). trade is complexity vs scale.

anna: can we capture the main ops playbook now? roughly:
- aggregator: short TTL, regional cert pool, per-tenant mTLS, strict quota per-agg, route automation for hairpin avoidance
- stub: tenant bootstrap module, health-check surface + local logs shipped to our console, MTU test during bootstrap

sam: +1. add a migration plan: move customers from aggregator -> stub when their egress or compliance triggers a tag. also policy for cutover: dual-write for 24h then flip.

infra-bot: deploy-checker: cp-aggregator-canary passed (integration tests: BGP adjacency, mTLS handshake, route propagation) — logs at <https://logs.company/12345>.

anna: thanks infra-bot. action items: i will write an RFC with the hybrid approach + canary rollout steps. please add any missing failure modes — e.g., IAM role limits for peering cross-account, ENI quotas, and observable alerts for asymmetric routing.

tara: add a synthetic test for hairpin and conntrack (we can run during canary). snippet that failed previously:
```
# tunnel on aggregator forced MSS clamp because of encapsulation
iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```

jess: also add cost thresholds to auto-propose stub migration (monthly egress > $X triggers review).

mohit: i'll draft the bootstrap terraform module for stubs and include an MTU check in user-data.

anna: perfect. i'll open RFC draft tomorrow and ping this thread. thanks everyone :pray:
